digest.en: Rubio lands in Europe as NATO allies weigh the Russian threat against the Middle East war. In Brazil, Flávio Bolsonaro’s surge signals a far-right shift despite Lula’s failures. Sudan’s top general meets a U.S. envoy in a rare bid to end the fighting.
digest.hi: नाइजीरिया के बोको शहर में आज सुबह एक एअरबस A320 का क्रैश हुआ, जिसमें 32 यात्रियों और क्रू के सभी सदस्य मारे गए। इसी दौरान यूरोप में यूक्रेन की सरकार ने अमेरिकी मध्यस्थता की मांग की, जबकि पुतिन ने वार्ता की बजाय सैन्य कार्रवाई को प्राथमिकता दी।

articles.title: U.S. envoy holds rare meeting with Sudan’s top general in push to seek end to fighting
articles.summary: Massad Boulos met with Abdel-Fattah Burhan in a rare diplomatic engagement. The U. S. envoy sought to pressure Sudan’s military leadership to negotiate an end to the ongoing conflict. This move aligns with broader efforts by the United States and Egypt to restart peace talks. The fighting has already killed at least 59,000 people. The rare meeting between Massad Boulos and Abdel-Fattah Burhan comes as the U. S., Egypt and other intermediaries seek to renew pressure on the warring parties in Sudan to negotiate an end to the fighting that has killed at least 59,000 people.

articles.title: Why Russia’s Baltic exclave is a new flashpoint
articles.summary: Moscow sent a formal diplomatic note to NATO accusing the alliance of increasing military pressure around Kaliningrad. Russia views these actions as attempts to isolate its Baltic exclave. NATO rejected the accusations, stating its regional activities remain strictly defensive. The exchange highlights growing friction over the strategic status of the territory. Moscow has accused the alliance of increasing military pressure around the strategic exclave and has sent a formal diplomatic note to the NATO over what it sees as attempts to isolate the territory; however, NATO has rejected the accusations, saying its activities in the region are ‘defensive’.

articles.title: Far right on the march and Lula’s failures: key drivers of Flávio Bolsonaro’s Brazil surge
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro won Brazil's first-round election, driven by evangelical support and President Lula's perceived rigidity. The 80-year-old incumbent's failures amplified the far-right surge. Rio's leftwing neighborhoods now chant for a political reversal. Experts say strength of evangelical church and stubbornness of Lula, 80, also helped propel Jair Bolsonaro’s son to first-round election winOn Sunday night, as the scale of the far-right triumph in Brazil sank in, an adapted football chant rang out in one of Rio’s most leftwing areas.“Let’s turn this around, Lu-laaaaa!

articles.title: Yemen, Saudi Arabia strike Houthis as counteroffensive gets underway
articles.summary: Yemeni forces launched a counteroffensive against Houthi-held Sanaa, executing over 1,000 strikes. The Saudi-led coalition supported the push with 100 warplane sorties at dawn. This marks a significant escalation in the regional conflict. The Yemeni military said it carried out more than 1,000 strikes and began an offensive against the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the internationally recognised government said 100 warplanes flew sorties at dawn.

articles.title: 'Don't You Have A Smart TV?': Iranian General's Smartwatch Defense Fuels Security Concerns
articles.summary: Iranian General Gholamreza Jalali faced backlash for wearing a smartwatch. He defended the choice by noting it is peacetime and citizens own smart TVs. The incident intensified criticism of lax security protocols among Iran’s senior military leadership. A photo of Brigadier General Gholamreza Jalali, the head of Iran's Passive Defense Organization, wearing a smartwatch has sparked a backlash. His response, that it's peacetime and people have smart TVs at home, has only fueled criticism of lax security among Iran's top brass.

articles.title: Protesters, Police Clash As Vote On President And Kosovo War Crimes Court Stalls
articles.summary: Kosovo’s parliament approved a bill to restrict the Hague tribunal’s jurisdiction. This occurred on October 5, the day before the presidential election deadline. Failure to elect a leader will trigger fresh parliamentary elections. Kosovo’s parliament approved at first reading a bill to sharply restrict the jurisdiction of the Hague-based Kosovo Specialist Chambers on October 5, a day before a deadline to elect a new president or face fresh parliamentary elections.

articles.title: Guardian readers fund life-changing surgery for Somali boy injured in US airstrike
articles.summary: Guardian readers funded life-saving surgery for Abdiqadir Salah, a seven-year-old Somali boy injured in a US drone strike. The operation took place in Mogadishu after an investigation revealed the attack killed twelve civilians. The boy’s mother described the hospital journey as a moment of mixed joy and apprehension. articles.title: Quebec poised to elect separatists to power for first time in more than a decade
articles.summary: Quebec voters are likely to elect the Parti Québécois to power for the first time in over a decade. The separatist party promises to hold an independence referendum by 2028. This would be the first such vote in Canada’s French-speaking region in many years. Parti Québécois promises to hold independence referendum in Canada’s French-speaking region by 2028Voters in Quebec are going to the polls in provincial elections which will probably result in victory for a party that has promised to hold a referendum on independence from Canada within the next two years. articles.title: Siberian Anti-Plague Institute Staff Isolated After Worker's Death
articles.summary: US officials monitor reports of a suspected pneumonic plague case in Russia’s Irkutsk region. A twenty-eight-year-old laboratory worker at the Siberian Anti-Plague Institute died, leading to staff isolation. Some US politicians now call for sweeping travel restrictions involving Russia. The United States is monitoring reports of a suspected case of pneumonic plague in Russia after the death of a 28-year-old laboratory worker in the Siberian region of Irkutsk, as some US political figures call for sweeping travel restrictions involving Russia.

articles.title: Rubio Heads To NATO Allies As Russian Threat, Middle East War Shape Agenda
articles.summary: Marco Rubio visits Iceland, Greece, and Portugal from October 5 to 8. He discusses security, defense, and energy with NATO partners. The agenda addresses Russian military activity and Middle East instability. These talks aim to strengthen allied cooperation on key strategic issues. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is heading to Iceland, Greece, and Portugal on October 5-8 for talks on security, defense, energy, economic cooperation, and technology as NATO allies face growing security concerns over Russia’s military activity and continued Middle East instability.

articles.title: Brazil presidential election 2026: first-round live results
articles.summary: Brazil holds its first-round presidential election, pitting incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva against Flávio Bolsonaro. The former president's son runs while his father remains imprisoned for plotting a coup. Candidates need over 50 percent of the vote to win outright. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is standing against Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of the presidential raceThe incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is up against Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is in prison for plotting a military coup.

articles.title: Nationalist Parties, Dodik Dominate Bosnian Election Amid Low Turnout
articles.summary: Milorad Dodik declared victory for his party in Bosnia's Serbian-led entity. Nationalist parties also won seats in the country's complex electoral system. Turnout was low. The results are likely to sustain high tensions across Bosnia and the wider region. Milorad Dodik, the Russia-friendly former leader of Bosnia-Herzegovina's Serbian-led entity, declared victory for his party in the region, with nationalist forces also scoring wins in Bosnia's complex electoral system -- results likely to keep tensions high in the country and the region.

articles.title: How a film brought a UN report to life in Xochimilco
articles.summary: A documentary based on United Nations University research screened at COP30 and European film festivals. The film returned to Xochimilco, the Mexico City canals where it was shot. This journey highlighted the local impact of the climate data presented in the report. A documentary drawn from United Nations University research was screened at the COP30 climate conference and film festivals across Europe.

articles.title: Bosnian Elections Pitted Pro-Western Against Nationalist Forces
articles.summary: Bosnian citizens voted on October 4 in elections for various political bodies. The contest pits pro-Western candidates against nationalist forces. Some candidates are pushing for faster integration into the European Union and NATO. Citizens in Bosnia-Herzegovina are casting their votes in elections to various bodies in the country’s multi-layered political system on October 4, with some candidates pushing for increased efforts at joining the European Union and NATO.

articles.title: Families Torn Apart, Trade At A Standstill: One Year Of The Afghan-Pakistan Border Closure
articles.summary: The Afghan-Pakistan border closure has lasted one year, halting cross-border trade. Tens of thousands of workers on both sides have lost their jobs. The shutdown has also disrupted commercial activity and strained family ties across the border. The prolonged closure of the Afghanistan-Pakistan border has brought cross-border trade to a standstill, leaving tens of thousands of people on both sides without work.

articles.title: Russia Strikes Kyiv Bridge As Merz Visits Ukrainian Capital
articles.summary: Russia warned foreign diplomats to leave Ukraine or face mortal danger as it vowed to escalate air strikes on Kyiv. President Zelenskyy stated Ukraine will respond to the intensified Kremlin campaign. The threat targets non-citizens currently in the country. Russia has vowed to intensify its relentless strikes against Kyiv and warned foreign diplomats and other visitors to leave the country or be exposed to “mortal danger,” while Ukraine's leader said his country will respond to the Kremlin's deadly air campaign.

articles.title: US Lawmakers Target Serbia's Democratic Backsliding, Ties To Russia, China, Iran
articles.summary: A bipartisan group of US lawmakers is demanding stricter measures against Serbia. They cite democratic backsliding, corruption, and expanding Russian, Chinese, and Iranian influence. The pressure arrives just weeks before snap parliamentary elections. A bipartisan, bicameral group of US lawmakers is pressing for tougher action on what they describe as democratic backsliding, corruption, and growing Russian, Chinese, and Iranian influence in Serbia, just weeks before snap parliamentary elections.

articles.title: Flydubai attack feeds Netanyahu’s ‘protector’ line as polls near
articles.summary: A Flydubai flight carrying 170 passengers faced an attempted hijacking. The pilot and passengers prevented a major disaster. Netanyahu released a video warning of threats shortly before the incident. The event reinforces his narrative of constant security risks for Israel. The apparent attempted hijacking of a Flydubai flight carrying 170 mostly Israeli passengers was another reminder to Israelis of the constant threat of terror and war.

articles.title: New F-16s buy Taiwan time and space against China’s air coercion
articles.summary: Taiwan received its first two F-16V Block 70 jets at Chihhang Air Base. The aircraft provide breathing room against Chinese gray-zone coercion. However, increasing Chinese stealth capabilities limit their wartime utility. The delivery marks a significant step in Taiwan's air defense strategy. Taiwan’s new American-made F-16V Block 70 jets deliver much-needed breathing room against daily Chinese gray-zone coercion, yet surging Chinese stealth numbers and cratered runway risks mean their wartime utility would be sharply contested.

articles.title: Row erupts over Cairo mural depicting Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin
articles.summary: Cairo authorities removed a 66-metre mural from Tahrir Square before Xi Jinping’s state visit. The artwork depicted Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin. Critics alleged it revived Afrocentric claims about Pharaohs’ origins. The removal sparked a public row over historical representation. articles.title: Arresting the Dangerous Descent Back into War in Northern Ethiopia
articles.summary: Armed groups in Tigray, Amhara, and Afar launched a multi-pronged offensive against Ethiopian forces. Long-simmering tensions have escalated into large-scale fighting. Analysts warn the situation risks a return to costly war. Diplomatic efforts remain necessary to avert further bloodshed in the region. Long-simmering tensions have turned to large-scale fighting after armed opposition groups in Tigray, Amhara and Afar launched a multi-pronged offensive against Ethiopian government forces.

articles.title: On Our Radar
articles.summary: Crisis Group's weekly radar highlights global conflicts and crises. Field experts identify under-reported trends and major developments. They explain why specific hotspots matter and outline necessary actions for stakeholders. On Our Radar scans conflicts and crises around the globe every week and features some of the hotspots Crisis Group’s analysts are closely watching. Whether an under-reported trend or a headline-grabbing development, our field experts explain why it matters or what should be done.

articles.title: The Houthis’ Advance to Bab al-Mandab: Has Yemen’s War Returned?
articles.summary: Crisis Group analyzed the rapid collapse of the Yemeni front near Bab al-Mandab. Experts discussed whether Saudi Arabia and regional neighbors can prevent escalation. The focus is on stopping the conflict from becoming a wider war. In this online event, Crisis Group and external experts discussed how the front collapsed so quickly and whether Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government and Yemen’s neighbours can keep this round of fighting from sliding into a wider war.

articles.title: पितरों की शांति का अनोखा विधान: पिशाचमोचन… घोड़े का कान, गाय की पूंछ और भैंस का सींग छूकर अकाल मौत
articles.summary: पिशाचमोचन पर संजाब नस्ल के दो घोड़े खड़े रहते हैं। ये घोड़े सालभर में सिर्फ श्राद्ध के पंद्रह दिन काम आते हैं। इनका उपयोग पितृपक्ष की शांति के लिए किया जाता है। पिशाचमोचन पर संजाब नस्ल के दो घोड़े पितृपक्ष के एक दिन पहले से खड़े हैं। इनका काम सालभर में सिर्फ श्राद्ध के 15 दिन होता है।
